limitations: Source rows and heldout panel are inherited by hash from the completed diverse-flow proposal.
Batch size 24 is the optimizer trace capacity; the first pass schedules six exact family groups, while later refills schedule only the deterministic complete-group prefix needed to reach 24.
Stages advance only on their optimizer target receipts; each stage has a finite two-times sampling-cycle refill cap and cannot mix leftover traces into the next stage.
Every admitted sampling attempt, including censored retries and bounded partial refills, increments the persisted per-stage counter bounded by the finite two-times refill cap.
Prime _maybe_batch remains closed until the binding admits the current complete group prefix, so a small carry-over deficit does not trigger a speculative 24-rollout refill.

Stale GroupCancellation voids all arrived members as explicit pipeline evidence and leaves no native pending IDs; only non-stale cancellation placeholders can contribute to a three-of-four admitted group.

Atomic JSON does not persist native TrainSink or Dispatcher buffers: partial cycle records, nonzero dispatch cursors, and admitted inventory without an exact selected-batch/update/tail-purge reconciliation fail closed; only clean optimizer/stage boundaries resume.

A censored cycle purges every native pending trace attributable to that cycle before its retry; restart reconciliation confirms only the exact expected applied policy version and fails closed on gaps.

The hash-bound preflight surface includes materialize.py, prepare_config.py, prepare_node.py, canary.py, launch.sh, run_from_sft.py, runtime_binding.py, sitecustomize.py, prime_tail_purge.py, and the reviewed external photo runner/trainer wrappers; canary and launch are prepared but not run.

The node-free Prime tail-purge adapter and run-owned runtime binding are tested against fake TrainSink/TrainSource/Dispatcher surfaces, but the Linux canary and full Prime compatibility remain pending; no launch-ready claim is made.
Anchors, renderer canary, model execution, rewards and visual judgments remain pending.

Bootstrap is prepared but unrun: it accepts only exact 1+1, 2+2, or 4+4 train/inference GPU topologies, including an 8-GPU whole-node offer split into four trainer and four inference GPUs; it uses public pinned downloads and the reviewed renderer sandbox helper, runs materialization/preflight/canary, and would write ready_no_launch without starting Prime; this preparation performed no downloads, hardware checks, network, or launch.

The receipt-derived launch_prepared.py handoff is prepared but unrun; it requires an explicit owner-only mode-600 gateway file and foreground timeout, validates receipts without reading or logging gateway contents, and performs no scheduling.

Pinned Prime source inspection verifies selected trace sequence_lengths and balanced_partition across four trainer workers; frozen-vision omission/offload has no supported hook, so launch remains fail-closed unless the preparation records an explicit trainer memory contract of at least 80 GiB. The real-backward canary remains unrun.

A real-backward canary is isolated under its unique launch-guards UUID: marker, config, output/checkpoint, rollout, cache, runtime state, failure receipt, and canary receipt stay outside the canonical full-run node paths.
